symptom: POST /checkout returns HTTP 500 'Something went wrong' for customers who signed in via SSO. Password-login customers are unaffected. Three confirmed failures since ~13:30 UTC on 2026-09-24, all business accounts. No charges to the card. requestId 7c4be913-checkout.
summary: SSO sessions are created with customer set to null (session.store.ts:16). The gateway middleware that lazily hydrates the customer profile checks customer === undefined (middleware.ts:21), so it skips hydration when customer is null — the wrong sentinel. When checkout calls PaymentService.charge, getBillingProfile reads session.customer (null), falls through to the cache (cold — loadProfile was never called for SSO logins), logs customer.billing_profile_missing, and returns null. The non-null assertion on payment.service.ts:24 suppresses the TypeScript error, and billing.defaultCardToken on line 25 crashes at runtime with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'defaultCardToken'). The crash propagates unhandled through CheckoutService.placeOrder and the gateway catch block returns HTTP 500. Password-login sessions call loadProfile during login (auth.service.ts:31) and set session.customer to a real profile, so they never hit the null branch. The minimal fix is changing the middleware null-check from === undefined to == null so that SSO sessions are hydrated on first request.

rootCause.title: SSO login leaves session.customer as null; middleware hydration guard checks === undefined, skipping null sessions
rootCause.explanation: SessionStore.create always initialises customer to null (session.store.ts:16). loginWithPassword immediately overwrites this with the loaded profile (auth.service.ts:31), but loginWithSso returns the session as-is without calling loadProfile (auth.service.ts:48-50). The gateway authenticate middleware is meant to lazily hydrate these sessions, but its guard is `if (session.customer === undefined)` (middleware.ts:21). Because null !== undefined, the hydration block is skipped entirely for every SSO session. Later, CustomerService.getBillingProfile checks `if (session.customer)` (customer.service.ts:26) — null is falsy, so it falls through to the in-process cache. The cache is also cold because loadProfile was never called for this customer in this server instance. The method logs customer.billing_profile_missing and returns null (customer.service.ts:28-30). Back in PaymentService.charge, the TypeScript non-null assertion `!` on line 24 (payment.service.ts:24) hides the null from the type checker; accessing billing.defaultCardToken on line 25 throws at runtime. The error is not an HttpError so the gateway catch block (server.ts:78-86) returns HTTP 500 with a generic message.

executionPath.label: SSO Login
executionPath.note: Session created with customer: null. loadProfile never called. session.save not called.

executionPath.label: Middleware Hydration
executionPath.note: Guard checks session.customer === undefined. SSO session has customer: null — condition is false. Hydration skipped.

executionPath.note: Inventory reserved. Calls payments.charge with session that has customer: null.

executionPath.label: PaymentService.charge
executionPath.note: getBillingProfile returns null. Non-null assertion ! suppresses TS error.

executionPath.note: billing is null. Accessing billing.defaultCardToken throws TypeError at runtime.

executionPath.label: Gateway 500
executionPath.note: Unhandled error catch block returns HTTP 500 internal_error.

evidence.text: Customer cus_2002 (business account) signed in through 'our company login' (SSO). Support could not reproduce with the support test account (password login). Two more tickets since 13:40 UTC, both business accounts.
Failing request identified: requestId 7c4be913-checkout. Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'defaultCardToken'), stack goes through PaymentService.charge.
Stack: TypeError at PaymentService.charge (payment.service.ts:25:31) at CheckoutService.placeOrder (checkout.service.ts:28:42) at async Object.handler (server.ts:60:21)
SessionStore.create always sets customer: null on new sessions.
loginWithPassword calls customers.loadProfile and assigns to session.customer (line 31), then sessions.save (line 32). loginWithSso does neither — session.customer stays null.
authenticate middleware hydration guard: `if (session.customer === undefined)`. SSO sessions have customer: null, so the guard is false and loadProfile is never called.
getBillingProfile: if session.customer is null (falsy), falls through to cache. Cache is cold for SSO sessions. Logs warning and returns null.
PaymentService.charge uses non-null assertion `!` on getBillingProfile result. If it returns null, accessing billing.defaultCardToken on line 25 throws TypeError at runtime.

ruledOut.hypothesis: Card processor (PSP) latency or timeout is the cause of the 500 error
ruledOut.reason: The PSP timeout appears only on requestId a1f09c2e-checkout (password login, log line 13), where attempt 1 timed out but attempt 2 succeeded (log line 14). requestId 7c4be913-checkout never emits psp.timeout or payment.charge_started — the crash happens before the PSP is contacted, at payment.service.ts:25 when billing is null. card-gateway.client.ts retries up to MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 and only throws after exhausting retries. PSP latency is a coincidence, unrelated to this incident.

ruledOut.hypothesis: Inventory low-stock or reservation failure causes the 500 error
ruledOut.reason: inventory.low_stock appears on requestId a1f09c2e-checkout (log line 10), not on the failing 7c4be913-checkout. For 7c4be913, inventory.reserved succeeds (log line 26) and inventory.released is logged (log line 29), correctly released in the catch block of CheckoutService.placeOrder (checkout.service.ts:35). An OutOfStockError would return 409, not a TypeError 500.

The smtp_degraded warning (log line 30) is emitted after billing_profile_missing and before checkout.failed — it belongs to the failure notification path in the catch block (checkout.service.ts:36). The checkout failure was already in progress. NotificationService queues emails when SMTP is degraded; it does not throw. The 500 is the TypeError from billing null dereference, not an SMTP failure.

ruledOut.hypothesis: Orders are being lost or customers are double-charged
ruledOut.reason: No charge was ever attempted for 7c4be913-checkout: the crash occurs at payment.service.ts:25 before gateway.charge is called. The customer's bank shows no pending authorisation (ticket line 19). The inventory reservation is released in the catch block (checkout.service.ts:35, confirmed by inventory.released log line 29). No order record is created. There is no data loss or double-charge risk for the failing requests.

ruledOut.hypothesis: The bug affects all authenticated customers, not just SSO users
ruledOut.reason: requestId a1f09c2e-checkout (password login, log line 3) completes successfully with status 201 (log line 17). loginWithPassword eagerly calls loadProfile (auth.service.ts:31) so session.customer is always a real CustomerProfile by checkout time. Only SSO sessions arrive at middleware with customer: null. All three failing tickets are business accounts, consistent with SSO being the enterprise login method.

fix.summary: Change the middleware hydration guard from `=== undefined` to `== null` so that SSO sessions (which have customer: null) are hydrated on their first authenticated request, as the comment on middleware.ts:17 describes. This is the minimal one-character fix. No schema or DB change required.
